messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify deleteNode correctly deletes a node with two children, replacing it with its inorder successor.
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the function handles the most complex BST deletion case, where the node to be deleted has two children, requiring correct successor replacement and subtree adjustment.

primary.name: deleteNode
primary.signature: struct node* deleteNode(struct node* root, int key)

dependencies.name: insert
dependencies.signature: struct node* insert(struct node* node, int key)
dependencies.reason: Used by helper_build_tree to construct test tree

assertions.name: assert_tree_inorder_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify the inorder traversal of the resulting tree matches the expected sequence after deletion.
assertions.usage: Check BST structure and contents after deletion

utilities.name: helper_build_tree
utilities.purpose: Builds a BST from an array of values for test setup.

utilities.name: helper_free_tree
utilities.purpose: Frees all nodes in the BST to prevent memory leaks.

data_structures: struct node* root (BST with at least one node having two children)
preconditions: BST is valid and contains the key to be deleted
Node to be deleted has both left and right children
setup_requirements.initial_state: BST with root node 50, left child 30, right child 70, and further children to ensure node 50 has two children

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to BST root with node 50 (two children)
primary_function_args.rationale: Ensures node 50 (root) has both left and right children, triggers two-child deletion path

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Key of node with two children (root: 50)
primary_function_args.rationale: Deletes node with two children, triggers path 6

return_value.description: Pointer to new root of BST (should be 60 after deletion)
return_value.validation: root pointer is not NULL and tree is valid BST

side_effects.effect: Node with key 50 is removed, replaced by its inorder successor (60)
side_effects.observable_via: Inorder traversal of tree matches expected sequence

state_changes: BST with root 50 → BST with root 60, all other nodes in correct BST order
invariants_maintained: All original nodes except 50 remain, 60 is now root

assertions_required.description: Verify inorder traversal matches expected after deleting node with two children
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Tree structure or contents incorrect after deletion

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All dynamically allocated nodes freed, no memory leaks

operation_sequence: Assert inorder traversal of result is [20, 30, 40, 60, 70, 80]
edge_cases_to_note: Successor node (60) may have a right child (none in this case, but test would still work if present)

path_coverage_analysis.description: Delete node with two children: replace with inorder successor, adjust right subtree

integration_test_suggestions: Test deleting a node with two children where the inorder successor itself has a right child.
Test deleting a node with two children that is not the root.
